data.name: Mallappa
data.gender_notes: Mallappa is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: God of Death, Lord of Yama
data.long_meaning: Mallappa is a Sanskrit name derived from the term 'Maha' meaning great and 'Lap' meaning death. In Hindu mythology, Mallappa is considered as the Lord of Yama, the Hindu god of death. He is also known as Maha-Yama or Yama Raja. The name Mallappa carries the meaning “God of Death, Lord of Yama” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mallappa usually hope their child will grow to embody god of death, lord of yama and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the cycle of birth and death, and the importance of living a virtuous life.
data.etymology: Mallappa belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Death, Lord of Yama.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mallappa total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mallappa holds significant cultural relevance in Hindu mythology as the name of a prominent deity associated with the concept of death and the afterlife. This name is often revered and invoked in rituals and ceremonies related to the deceased, particularly in the regions where Yama or Maha-Yama is highly revered.
data.spiritual_significance: Mallappa represents the greatness of the cyclical nature of life and death. It is a reminder that life continues even after physical death and that the supreme consciousness continues to exist. The name is a symbol of acceptance and surrender to the natural order of things, signifying a deep spiritual understanding and connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mallappa: Worshipper of Mallikarjuna, the Lord of Arjuna. Symbolizes deep devotion and dedication towards the supreme deity. Spiritually, it represents the journey towards attaining divine grace and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that King Mallappa Nayaka of the Keladi Nayaka Kingdom in Karnataka, India. He ruled from 1652 to 1664. The name Mallappa carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mallappa was an accomplished military leader who extended the territorial control of the Keladi Nayaka Kingdom in Karnataka during his reign. He is known for his victory against the Bijapur Sultanate in the Battle of Sagara Karnataka in 1659.

historical_references.reference: Mallappa Swamy, a popular Hindu deity in the village of Melkote in Karnataka, India. The temple dedicated to him is considered a significant pilgrimage site.
historical_references.context: Mallappa Swamy, also known as Mallandevu or Mallikarjuna Swamy, is a form of Lord Shiva. The temple dedicated to him in Melkote is believed to have been established in the 13th century. The deity is known for his blessings to childless couples and is revered for granting children.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Mallappa' is of Hindu origin and is commonly found in the Indian state of Karnataka. In contemporary times, the name has gained popularity in various contexts. On Twitter, Mallappa is often discussed in the context of Karnataka politics, particularly in relation to the Mallikarjuna Swamy temple in Srisailam. On Instagram, Mallappa is a popular name for pet dogs, with many users sharing pictures and stories of their furry friends named Mallappa. In the world of literature, Mallappa is a recurring character in historical fiction, often portrayed as a brave and just ruler in stories set in medieval India.
